title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 348 (Information as to pending liquidations)

content.overview: If the winding up of a company is not concluded within one year after its commencement, the Company Liquidator shall, unless exempted wholly or in part by the Central Government, within two months of the expiry of that year and thereafter at intervals of not more than one year (or shorter prescribed intervals), file a statement in the prescribed form, containing the prescribed particulars and duly audited by a person qualified to act as auditor of the company, with respect to the proceedings in and position of the liquidation: with the Tribunal (Tribunal winding up) or with the Registrar (voluntary winding up). A copy of a Tribunal filing is also filed with the Registrar. Creditors and contributories may inspect and obtain copies on payment of the prescribed fee.
content.glance: If winding up exceeds one year, Liquidator must file periodic audited statements of proceedings and position with Tribunal/Registrar; creditors/contributories may inspect.
content.study: Section 348 imposes ongoing reporting for protracted liquidations. If the winding up is not concluded within one year of commencement, the Company Liquidator must (unless exempted by the Central Government) file within two months of the year-end and thereafter at intervals not exceeding one year (or shorter if prescribed) a prescribed-form statement of the proceedings and position of the liquidation, duly audited by a person qualified to act as auditor of the company. Filing is with the Tribunal in Tribunal winding up and with the Registrar in voluntary winding up; a copy of a Tribunal filing goes to the Registrar. Creditors and contributories stating themselves as such in writing may inspect and take copies on payment of the prescribed fee. Audit is not required where s. 294 applies.

sections.heading: Periodic statement
sections.body: If not concluded within one year, audited statement of proceedings and position to be filed at prescribed intervals with Tribunal or Registrar.

sections.heading: Inspection
sections.body: Creditors and contributories may inspect and obtain copies on payment of fee.

examples.title: Overrun liquidation
examples.body: A Tribunal winding up has run for 18 months. The Company Liquidator files the annual audited statement under s. 348 with the Tribunal and a copy with the Registrar.

hypotheticals.question: Is the annual statement required if the winding up finishes within one year?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The duty arises only if the winding up is not concluded within one year after commencement.

misconceptions.trap: The Liquidator need not report if creditors do not demand it.
misconceptions.correction: The duty is statutory and periodic once the one-year threshold is crossed, subject to Central Government exemption.
